title: Linear + ReLU
summary: A tiny two-row dense layer applies PyTorch’s output-by-input weight layout, adds a per-output bias, then clamps negative activations to zero.
example:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

x = torch.tensor([[1, 2, -1], [0.5, -2, 3]])
weight = torch.tensor([[0.25, -0.5, 1], [-1, 0.5, 0.25]])
bias = torch.tensor([0.1, 0.6])
layer = torch.nn.Linear(3, 2)
with torch.no_grad():
    layer.weight.copy_(weight)
    layer.bias.copy_(bias)
y = F.relu(layer(x))
limitations: Fixed fixture: batch=2, input features=3, output features=2; weights use PyTorch [out_features, in_features] order.
The CUDA teaching kernel is a scalar, unfused-equivalent illustration for this fixture, not PyTorch dispatch, autograd, or a performance model.

tensors.description: Two input rows with three features.

tensors.description: Two output neurons; each row contains three weights.

stages.title: Dense dot product
stages.summary: Each output thread chooses its batch row and output column, then reduces three feature-wise products.
stages.insight: The weight matrix is stored output-major, so output column o reads contiguous W[o, :].

stages.title: Bias and ReLU
stages.summary: The bias is included in the accumulator; ReLU preserves positive values and maps negative values to zero.
stages.insight: The fixture includes both clipped and surviving outputs so the activation is visible.
